angle: He opens Daily Word as a man before he opens it as a pastor. So the screen gives him his own reading first and one door to Sunday second — and every source, human or AI, says where it came from.
thesis: Today the pastor's Home says "this is your time — not ministry, just you and God" (persona-config.ts:253) and then puts the Preach card above the reading (HomeScreen.tsx:2106) and a four-tile campus dashboard below it. The layout argues with the greeting. The fix is not fewer things — Ashley's look is rich, and stripping it once got reverted — it is order and honesty: his reading and his reflection at the top, one card called For Sunday underneath that carries what he has actually filed, and a named source on every commentary, lexicon and AI answer. Barna gives the reason (65% of pastors report loneliness, up from 42% in 2015; 38% considered quitting in the past year) and the guardrail (79% worry AI could replace God's role, 63% pastoral leadership) — the app that keeps a pastor is the one that feeds him before it asks him to produce, and never sounds like it wants the pulpit.
principles: His soul first, Sunday second, on one screen, in that order. Everything ministry-facing lives below the reading and the reflection — that is also the standing ruling (Sermon Notes row demoted below the reading for pastor_leader, PR #82).
One door, not a dashboard. Numbers with no action do not belong on a devotional screen. The campus figures keep one live line in the For Sunday card and their full view on the Campus tab.
Never ask for what sign-in already knows. The campus pastor code is SHA-256(campusId + PASTOR_SECRET) and the client cannot derive it — sign-in mints it. So Home offers sign-in, never a code box.
A study aid that hands him material and names where it came from. It never writes the message and never claims a reference it cannot show.
Count what he did; never estimate, never shame. Filed passages are a real number. "Minutes saved" is not, until dw_events exists.
Comfort is one tap from this path and never changes the path. No graduation prompt, ever; the comfort toolbar stays Note and Close only.
Rich, warm, editorial. Photo hero, white paper reading panel, terracotta and ivory, Georgia serif. Nothing greyed out, nothing stripped.

journey.day0: He taps the path swatch or the landing line, sees one sheet — "Where are you today?" — and taps "I'm a pastor and I teach and preach". One tap saves it as a real choice and opens Home immediately; no CTA below the fold. Home lands with today's chapter already open, seeded credit-free (never through handleRead). If no plan is running, the hero serves a rotating leadership chapter so the screen is never empty, and the set-up row now says so in plain words instead of leaving him to guess why a chapter is there. Nothing blocks him: not the wizard, not sign-in, not email.
journey.first_session: Reads the open chapter with commentary expanded (his feature, kept). Under it, Between You & God asks one question written for leaders. Two actions — Journal this, Talk it through — plus one quiet new line: "Heavy week? Open the comfort readings." Below that, the For Sunday card, empty and honest: "Nothing filed yet — highlight a verse and tap To sermon. It lands here." He taps Mark as read; the streak records once; the push ask comes after, not before, and never stacks with anything else.
journey.return_visit: Same shape, more in it. Greeting counts the days in his own register. The chapter is open again. Any verse he highlighted and filed shows as a count on the For Sunday card — the card now has a reason to be tapped. If he has signed in, one line reads "Gwinnett · 34 reading today" and taps through to the Campus tab; if he has not, it reads "Sign in as pastor to see your campus" — a link, not a code box.
journey.week2: He has a plan running, so Today's Study replaces the set-up row, with the Greek and Hebrew toggle he already has. For Sunday carries his preaching focus as its title and the filed count as its sub-line: "Romans 8 — the mind set on the Spirit · 7 passages filed". Tapping it opens Pastors Sermon Prep with everything already in the bag. On Monday, the week-in-review card appears (moved off Sunday, which is his workday) with two counts and one question. Bible AI's "For your message" block is where he goes for angles, and every answer carries the line that tells him to check the reference.
journey.missed_day: Nothing turns red and nothing scolds. The streak engine already grants one freeze, replenished after seven days — it just spends it silently today. It now says so once, plainly: "You missed a day. The streak held." Past two days the greeting falls back to the low-streak pastor line, which is already the warmest one in the file. The For Sunday card still shows everything he filed, so no work looks lost. No push mentions a streak, ever.
journey.seasonal: When Futures runs a church-wide read — New Year, Lent, a series — the For Sunday card carries it: "Futures is reading Mark together · Day 4 of 21", and the Campus tab shows how many at his campus are on it. This is the one place a campus number does work: it tells him whether his people came with him. Calendar moments are where the spikes are (3M+ one-year-plan starts on 1 Jan 2025; 21.6M opens on Easter 2026; Hallow hit 5M concurrent in Pray40).

comfort_access: One quiet line at the foot of the Between You & God card: "Heavy week? Open the comfort readings. Your path stays where it is." It opens the comfort reading in comfortMode — toolbar is Note and Close only, no streak, no completion, no count, no graduation prompt ever. It must NOT call saveSetup, so his saved path, his plan, his filed bag and his campus tools are all untouched; when he closes it he is back on the pastor Home exactly where he left. The research is blunt about why this belongs on every path rather than only the comfort door: crisis is not a persona someone chooses on a good day. For this persona it is also the highest-duty-of-care move in the app — 65% of pastors report loneliness, up from 42% in 2015, and 38% considered quitting in the past year. If he types crisis language into Study help or a prayer request, the safety flow applies here as everywhere: confirm gently, then show the region-correct line (988 in the US, 13 11 14 in Australia, 0800 543 354 in New Zealand) and the human next step, with the first-use disclosure that this is scripture and a church, not counselling.
reminders: One a day, no more. The hour is inferred from his own behaviour after five sessions — the median local hour at which he actually opens — and only then; before that it is the hour he set, or none. Copy is verse-first and neutral: "Romans 8 is open when you are." Never a streak threat, never a guilt frame, because guilt-framed streak reminders are what drive notification opt-out and uninstall. Two pastor-specific rules: nothing fires on a Sunday before noon, because that is his heaviest working morning; and nothing fires at all in the two hours before his campus's service time when the app knows it. A missed day produces no extra push — the streak freeze already covers one day, and it now says so in the app once he opens. Push is verifiable only on futuresdailyword.com, www or localhost, never on a deploy preview or the church proxy, so the check for this work happens on prod. All templates and verse snippets should move out of the hardcoded arrays in push-send.js so wording and language change without a function deploy.
instrumentation: dw_events table plus a nightly rollup — this is build step one. No public source will ever supply D1/D7/D30 for a Bible app, so nothing below can be judged without it.
pastor_home_open {signed_in, has_plan, has_focus, filed_count} — the D1/D7/D30 curve for this path, and whether sign-in correlates with return.
reading_seeded then reading_marked {ref} — the honest conversion of arrival-open into a finished reading. The seed must stay credit-free; this event is the only thing that should know it happened.
pastor_reflect_shown / pastor_reflect_journal / pastor_reflect_talk — does Between You & God get used, or only seen. The loneliness hypothesis stands or falls here.
comfort_open {from: 'pastor_leader'} — reach of the cross-path comfort tap, and whether it ever precedes a lapse.
sermon_file_item {ref} — filed passages per week. This is the real 'work done' number and the only one honest enough to display.

for_sunday_open {filed_count, has_focus} and prep_return {gap_seconds} — hand-off rate, and whether he comes back to Daily Word after Sermon Prep. prep_return is the check on the off-scope navigation.
ai_pastor_prompt {kind} — which of the four prompts earn their place; already tracked locally as trackBehavior('ai_prompt','pastor:kind') but it never reaches the server.
study_source_open — does the trust panel get tapped once the source line exists. Tests the research claim directly.
reminder_sent / reminder_open / reminder_off — opt-out rate is the shame signal. Watch it against the copy change, not in isolation.
streak_freeze_spent — how often grace is doing the work, and whether surfacing it changes return.
campus_view_open — whether campus numbers are wanted at all once they are one tap away instead of on the devotional screen.

Every one of these must be added to the TRACKED_EVENTS allowlist in src/utils/analytics.ts or it is silently dropped. Ship the allowlist entry and the call in the same commit, and add a test that fails when they diverge.
self_serve_levers: Between You & God prompts — move the 15-line array out of persona-config.ts into public/books/pastor-prompts.json. /books/* is already network-first with cache as offline fallback, so an edit reaches returning readers on their second open with no deploy. Preaching focus — already self-serve (dw_sermon_prep_focus); the For Sunday card just needs to expose the edit, so a pastor names what he is preaching without opening Sermon Prep.
Campus corner line — already self-serve. A campus pastor posts through /staff intake and it appears; no dev, no ticket.
Sunday's congregation notes — already self-serve from Sermon Prep through intake (format_preview, confirm, submit), landing in Daily Word's Sermon Notes.
Campus and path — already self-serve on Home: the campus chip applies on tap, the path swatch opens the one sheet.
Reminder hour and on/off — already self-serve in Settings, backed by preferred_hour on push_subscriptions.

Adding a NEW campus still needs a developer (CAMPUSES in src/data/tokens.ts). Design it out by reading the campus list from the staff roster that already assigns campuses — then a campus exists in the app the moment it exists on the roster.

Plan ids stay a four-file rule (personalization.ts, SetupPromptModal.tsx, PlansScreen.tsx, PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx). Do not turn that into a lever — add a test that fails when an id appears in fewer than four places, so the wizard can never start a dead plan.

open_decisions: Do the four Campus Overview tiles leave the Home screen for the Campus tab, with one live line staying in the For Sunday card? This is an IA reshape of the opening screen and is his call on a preview, not a build decision.

Should the For Sunday hand-off open Pastors Sermon Prep in a new window so Daily Word survives behind it, or keep the current full navigation he ruled on 9 Sep? An installed PWA that navigates off-scope can leave a pastor with no way back.
Does the pastor's week-in-review move to Monday, or does he want it dropped? It renders nothing today either way, so a decision is needed before the flag stops lying.
Who may edit /books/pastor-prompts.json — Ashley only, or campus pastors through the staff site? That decides whether it is a file he owns or an intake surface.
Is the pastor tier flat-priced or a subscription? The research points at real backlash against recurring cost in this market, and pricing shapes what the app is allowed to gate.
Once dw_events exists, do we compute and show 'minutes from open to outline'? The research asks for it; some pastors will read a timer on their devotional life as surveillance.
Should any push ever reach a pastor on a Sunday, or is the whole day off by default for this persona?
risks: This is the class of change that got PR #80 reverted with 'you have completely stripped, go back'. Moving the Preach card and the campus tiles must land on a preview link, with the screen visibly richer than before, and must not merge without his word.

The pastor arrival strip copy currently ends 'Preach is the card above'. If the card moves and that string does not, in all four languages, the app lies to him in the first sentence he reads on the new layout.

Removing the four campus tiles from Home can read as gutting. Mitigate by making For Sunday carry more than the old card did — focus, filed count, campus line, church-wide read — so the screen gains weight where it loses a grid.

Editing pastor content in /books is invisible to returning users unless the service worker strategy for that asset class holds. /books/* must stay network-first with cache as offline fallback; bump CACHE_NAME/STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION together for any sw.js change.
Touching persona-config sectionOrder for pastor_leader risks the tests that pin the other four personas. Change one persona's array per commit and run the whole suite, not the pastor specs alone.
features.weeklyReview: true with no mounted component is a half-existing feature. Mount it or drop the flag — do not leave a third state.

The arrival seed must keep bypassing handleRead. Any refactor of the hero that routes the seed through the read path silently credits a plan day and corrupts the streak evidence this design depends on.

Never rebuild a synced dw_* record from React state. The filed bag and the focus ride the misc bag; merge into what is currently in localStorage and touch only your own fields, or a second device's progress is overwritten by stale mount-time state.
Deploy previews return 403 from the app's own /api, so scripture falls back to offline KJV and push does not exist there. Verify translations, study sources and reminders on prod, not on the preview.
If instrumentation ships after the copy changes, none of the framing claims can be judged and the next round of design is guesswork again.
